## Objective

Deliver one consistent intent-discovery procedure and supporting package content.

## Scope

- Rewrite the entry behavior and metadata
- Define the detailed adaptive discovery procedure
- Add concise interaction examples
- Align the document contract and template explanation
- Update the synthetic example and dependent clarification fixture
- Align package documentation and version references
- Align the focused package contract checks

## Entry conditions

- Baseline and scenario definition phase is complete.
- The three proposed decisions have been resolved through exact-plan review.

## Exit criteria

- Entry, references, examples, metadata and maintenance docs agree.
- The example and relevant fixtures match the preserved schema and semantics.
- Protected helper, attribution and license remain unchanged.

## Risks

- Avoid duplicated procedures, unsupported design choices, schema drift and silent fixture no-ops.

### Risks

- Critical rules placed only behind links may never be applied.
- An absolute local rule must not override higher-priority host constraints or current user authority.

### Acceptance criteria

- The entry file carries the critical discovery-to-synthesis controls, one-material-question default, actual waiting, changed-answer handling, and authorized-save boundaries.
- The metadata accurately describes discovery while retaining the to-trd name, TRP alias meaning, explicit invocation and existing-role boundary.
- Fast-path eligibility, draft-now behavior, no-follow-up limits, exact-revision approval and current completion diagnostics remain explicit without a second lifecycle or compulsory interview.

### Planned verification

- Review each entry branch against REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-004–REQ-010 and REQ-015 acceptance.
- Validate the existing frontmatter and metadata package checks and inspect description lengths and explicit-invocation policy.
- Compare the changed text with the existing authority and lifecycle clauses to confirm preservation.

### Risks

- A detailed procedure can contradict the entry flow or repeat questions that the user has already answered.

### Acceptance criteria

- The detailed procedure implements the entry flow with applicability-based readiness and explicit handling of partial answers, invalidated branches, no-follow-up restrictions, and requested incomplete drafts.
- Sources establish facts but not user preferences; proposed designs and delegated choices retain their actual authority status.
- The pre-save review distinguishes unresolved current-task intake from legitimate questions that are part of the deliverable.

### Planned verification

- Walk C01–C11 against the written control flow and inspect every ordinary save boundary.
- Check that clarification changes the affected requirement and acceptance and that unresolved intake is not delegated under another heading.
- Compare the entry and reference to resolve any competing instruction or redundant confirmation requirement.
